personas.summary: Not-go as written; this needs a revision pass before I would assign it. The underlying chemistry is mostly sound — I machine-verified all 13 asset SMILES and every structure inside all 32 questions with RDKit (formulas, InChIKeys, CIP labels) and found no invalid or misidentified compound, and I re-derived every answer key and found the intended outcomes correct. But two graded items are chemically wrong as depicted: ch8-epox-product-v2 keys a single enantiomer (2R,3R, InChIKey PQXKWPLDPFFDJP-QWWZWVQMSA-N) as THE product of epoxidizing achiral (E)-2-butene with an achiral peroxyacid, when the reaction must give the racemate and the equally correct (2S,3S) answer is neither offered nor accepted; and ch8-diol-syn keys an option labeled 'A syn (cis) 1,2-diol' whose drawn structure is OCCO, ethane-1,2-diol, a molecule with no stereocenters that cannot be cis or anything else. Beyond those, the deeper instructional problem is that this is a reaction chapter with no reactions in it: every one of the six sections presents a substrate molecule and a product molecule as two unlinked static blocks with no arrow, no reagents, and no mechanism, even though five of the six nuggets are typed 'mechanism' and the prose names intermediates (organoborane, five-membered osmate ester, ozonide, concerted oxygen transfer) that are never drawn. Worse, all three reactions whose entire teaching point is stereochemistry are illustrated on substrates where the stereochemistry is invisible — but-2-ene to butane, propene to methyloxirane, propene to propane-1,2-diol — so a student can read the whole chapter and never once see what 'syn' looks like. Assessment breadth is genuinely strong (32 items, 11 question types, every concept covered, targeted wrong-answer feedback and hint ladders throughout), but several graded answers depend on content this chapter never teaches (epoxide anti ring-opening, 9-BBN, hot concentrated KMnO4, alkyne hydrogenation), two prompts state their own answers, and all six practice_checks vanish in compilation — the reader a student actually sees contains zero retrieval practice. Four of the six 'background reading' links in the compiled reader return HTTP 404.

location.anchor_text: trans-2,3-dimethyloxirane (the trans epoxide)

findings.observation: The keyed-correct option is [redacted — specific enantiomer], which RDKit resolves to a single, fully specified enantiomer: (2R,3R)-2,3-dimethyloxirane (InChIKey [redacted]). (E)-2-butene is achiral and mCPBA is achiral, so the reaction cannot produce a single enantiomer — it must give a racemic 1:1 mixture of (2R,3R) and (2S,3S). The (2S,3S) enantiomer (InChIKey [redacted]) is neither offered as an option nor listed in answer_key.correct_option_ids, so a student who correctly reasons to the other enantiomer of the trans epoxide has no way to be right. The cis distractor [redacted] is correctly the meso (2R,3S) isomer, and the trans/cis labels themselves are correct, so the defect is specifically the single-enantiomer depiction and keying, not the syn/stereospecificity teaching point.
findings.learner_impact: Students in Organic 1 form the durable misconception that an achiral alkene plus an achiral oxidant can deliver one enantiomer. This is precisely the misconception the reaction-stereochemistry section of a standard chapter 8 exists to prevent, and it will have to be un-taught when optical activity and racemates are formalized. Students who write the (2S,3S) answer are marked wrong for correct chemistry.
findings.evidence: ch8-epox-product-v2 student_config.options[0].structure_smiles [redacted]; RDKit rdCIPLabeler gives atom 1 = R, atom 3 = R. answer_key [redacted]. No nugget in the package mentions racemic products or the stereochemical consequence of achiral reagents.
findings.recommended_outcome: The chapter needs the epoxidation stereochemistry item to represent the actual product composition — a racemate, not one enantiomer — and it needs the accompanying principle (achiral starting material plus achiral reagent cannot give a single enantiomer) stated somewhere in the prose that the item draws on.

location.anchor_text: A syn (cis) 1,2-diol

findings.observation: The keyed-correct option carries a stereochemistry label [redacted] attached to a structure [redacted] that is actually achiral ethane-1,2-diol. Ethylene glycol has no stereocenters and no cis/trans relationship whatsoever; calling it a syn (cis) diol is a false statement of chemistry that the student sees rendered next to the correct answer. Compounding it, the 'anti (trans) 1,2-diol' distractor (option b) carries no structure at all, so the two options a student is asked to discriminate between on stereochemical grounds are presented asymmetrically — one with an irrelevant drawing, one with nothing.
findings.learner_impact: The one graded item that introduces the syn-diol concept teaches, visually, that any vicinal diol is 'syn.' Students who reason from the picture rather than the words conclude that syn/anti is a property of the connectivity (two adjacent OH groups) rather than of the face of delivery, which is exactly the trouble_spot the concept declares ('Assigning anti stereochemistry to a syn addition'). It also makes option b unselectable on visual grounds and cues the answer non-chemically.
findings.evidence: ch8-diol-syn student_config.options[0] = {'id':'a','text':'A syn (cis) 1,2-diol','structure_smiles':'OCCO'}; options[1] = {'id':'b','text':'An anti (trans) 1,2-diol'} with no structure_smiles; answer_key [redacted]. RDKit: OCCO has zero stereocenters (CIP=[]).
findings.recommended_outcome: The syn/anti discrimination item needs structures on which syn and anti are actually distinguishable and drawn, applied consistently to every option in the set, so the visual a student grades against agrees with the stereochemical label it carries.

location.anchor_text: Which reagent system converts cyclopentene into cis-cyclopentane-1,2-diol?

findings.observation: The prompt asks specifically for the cis diol, but the structure attached to the correct reagent option is 'OC1CCCC1O' — cyclopentane-1,2-diol with no stereochemistry specified (RDKit: no CIP codes, no wedge/dash information). The cis (meso) isomer would require defined relative configuration. The distractor options b and c carry no structures at all.
findings.learner_impact: The one item in the chapter that could show a student what a cis ring diol looks like shows an undifferentiated flat structure instead. A student trying to check their stereochemical reasoning against the rendered answer gets no confirmation, and the cis/trans distinction that the whole question turns on is never made visible.
findings.evidence: ch8-diol-syn-v2 student_config.options[0] = {'id':'a','text':'OsO₄, then NaHSO₃','structure_smiles':'OC1CCCC1O'}; RDKit CIP = [] (no stereocenters assigned). Prompt text names 'cis-cyclopentane-1,2-diol' explicitly.
findings.recommended_outcome: Where a question's answer turns on cis versus trans, the depicted structure needs to carry the relative configuration; the chapter needs its ring-diol example to show the cis relationship rather than leaving it undefined.

location.anchor_text: Identify the alkane formed by syn addition of H2 to but-2-ene.

findings.observation: All three reactions in this chapter whose central teaching point is stereochemistry are illustrated with substrate/product pairs on which the stereochemistry is undetectable. Hydrogenation: but-2-ene (CC=CC, no E/Z even specified) to butane (CCCC) — butane is achiral with no stereocenters, so syn versus anti delivery gives literally the same molecule. Epoxidation: propene (CC=C) to 2-methyloxirane (CC1CO1) — one stereocenter, so stereospecificity is invisible. Dihydroxylation: propene to propane-1,2-diol (CC(O)CO) — one stereocenter, so syn and anti addition give the identical (racemic) product. The asset learning_goals nonetheless assert the stereochemistry ('the alkane formed by syn addition', 'the vicinal (1,2) diol from syn dihydroxylation of propene').
findings.learner_impact: A student can read the entire chapter, look at every figure, and never once see what 'syn addition' produces. The word 'syn' remains a label attached to a reagent rather than a spatial claim about a product, which is exactly why students later assign anti stereochemistry to OsO4 or forget that both hydrogens land on one face. The declared trouble_spots for catalytic-hydrogenation and syn-dihydroxylation both name this failure mode, and no figure in the chapter counters it.
findings.evidence: assets mol-hydrog-butene (CC=CC) / mol-butane (CCCC); mol-propene-ep (CC=C) / mol-methyloxirane (CC1CO1); mol-propene-diol (CC=C) / mol-propane-1-2-diol (CC(O)CO). RDKit confirms zero stereocenters in CCCC and a single stereocenter in CC1CO1 and CC(O)CO. nugget-hydrogenation prose: 'for a disubstituted alkene the two new carbon–hydrogen bonds are formed on the same side' — no figure shows this.
findings.recommended_outcome: Each syn-addition concept needs at least one worked substrate on which the two faces are actually distinguishable (a cyclic or 1,2-disubstituted alkene), so that the stereochemical claim in the prose is something a student can see and reproduce rather than memorize.

location.anchor_text: form a five-membered cyclic osmate ester

findings.observation: Five of the six nuggets carry type 'mechanism', but no mechanism appears anywhere in the package or the compiled reader — there is not a single curved arrow, transition state, or intermediate structure. The prose names four intermediates as the causal explanation for the observed outcome and draws none of them: the five-membered cyclic osmate ester (nugget-dihydroxylation), the organoborane and its concerted four-centre addition (nugget-hydroboration), the ozonide (nugget-ozonolysis), and the concerted oxygen transfer from the peroxyacid O–O bond (nugget-epoxidation). Because the cyclic intermediate IS the reason for syn delivery, removing it reduces every stereochemical claim in the chapter to an assertion.
findings.learner_impact: Students are given the outcome ('syn because a cyclic ester forms on one face') without the object that makes it inevitable, so the chapter becomes a reagent-to-product lookup table. This is the memorization failure mode: students who cannot picture the osmate ester have no way to reconstruct syn selectivity under exam pressure, and no basis for predicting a reaction they have not memorized. It also leaves ch8-stereo-categorize's hint ('Reactions through a cyclic intermediate on one face are syn') pointing at something the chapter never showed.
findings.evidence: nuggets nugget-hydrogenation, nugget-hydroboration, nugget-epoxidation, nugget-dihydroxylation, nugget-ozonolysis all have type='mechanism'. The compiled reader contains only block_type 'text', 'molecule', 'reaction_coordinate', 'video' (hidden), 'external_link', 'mcmurry_link'. The only non-molecule figure in the whole chapter is rc-epoxidation.
findings.recommended_outcome: The mechanism-typed sections need the intermediates and the electron flow their own prose relies on to be visible, so that syn delivery, retention at the boron-bearing carbon, and complete C=C cleavage are derivable rather than asserted.

location.anchor_text: Hydroboration substrate: 1-butene

findings.observation: In the compiled reader, every transformation is presented as two independent molecule blocks with no connecting arrow, no reagents or conditions over an arrow, and no combined caption. For example, section nugget-hydroboration renders blk-2zpgo66v ('Hydroboration substrate: 1-butene') followed by blk-udsl7aee ('Anti-Markovnikov product: butan-1-ol') as two separate figures; nothing in the figure layer states BH3-THF then H2O2/NaOH. The same pattern holds in all six sections. The chapter therefore contains zero reaction schemes.
findings.learner_impact: Students learn reactions as substrate-product pairs to be matched rather than as transformations with conditions, which is why reagent-recall questions like ch8-reagent-match and ch8-synth-route feel disconnected from the reading. It also means the reagent strings a student is graded on (BH3.THF; H2O2/NaOH; OsO4 then NaHSO3; O3 then Zn) appear only in question text, never in the chapter's figures.
findings.evidence: Compiled reader sections nugget-hydrogenation, nugget-hydroboration, nugget-epoxidation, nugget-dihydroxylation, nugget-ozonolysis, nugget-synthesis — every asset is type 'molecule' with a standalone SMILES; assets[] contains no reaction-scheme asset of any kind. Reagent strings appear only in question_sets student_config.
findings.recommended_outcome: Each reaction section needs its transformation shown as one connected scheme carrying substrate, arrow, reagents/conditions, and product, so the reading and the assessment refer to the same object.

location.anchor_text: When an epoxide is opened by aqueous acid, water attacks from the opposite face

findings.observation: Several graded answers depend on chemistry this chapter never teaches. (1) ch8-epox-diol-name and ch8-stereo-categorize (item i_epox, keyed to g_anti) both require anti stereochemistry of epoxide ring-opening; the epoxidation nugget says only that 'the ring can afterward be opened by a range of nucleophiles under either basic or acidic conditions' and never states the stereochemistry, and the alkene-epoxidation concept lists only 'alkene-structure-pi-bond' as a prerequisite. Epoxide opening lives in the downstream 'epoxides'/'ethers-epoxides-thiols-and-sulfides' packages. (2) ch8-antimarkovnikov-select keys 9-BBN as correct; 9-BBN appears nowhere in any nugget. (3) ch8-stereo-categorize-v2 keys hot concentrated KMnO4 as a cleaving reagent; the prose mentions only cold, dilute, basic KMnO4 for syn dihydroxylation. (4) ch8-hydrog-equiv-v2 grades alkyne hydrogenation (propyne, 2 equiv); alkynes are a later chapter and are not a listed prerequisite.
findings.learner_impact: A student who has read this chapter carefully and mastered its objectives will still miss these items, and will not know whether the gap is their understanding or the reading. Instructors assigning the bank as written will field complaints, and the misses land disproportionately on the advanced-difficulty items that are meant to discriminate real synthetic reasoning.
findings.evidence: ch8-epox-diol-name answer_key [redacted]; ch8-stereo-categorize answer_key [redacted]; ch8-antimarkovnikov-select answer_key [redacted] where b = '9-BBN, then H2O2 / NaOH'; ch8-stereo-categorize-v2 correct_assignments.i_hotkmno4 = 'g_cleave'; ch8-hydrog-equiv-v2 prompt 'propyne (CH3-C#CH)'. None of '9-BBN', 'hot', 'alkyne', or the anti stereochemistry of ring-opening appears in any nuggets[].text.
findings.recommended_outcome: Either the chapter needs to teach these four points (anti ring-opening, bulky boranes, hot versus cold permanganate, alkyne reduction stoichiometry) or the items that grade them need to be scoped out; as it stands the assessment measures content the chapter does not deliver.

location.anchor_text: giving a 1,2-diol whose two -OH groups are on opposite faces. What one-word (or two-word) term describes the stereochemical relationship

findings.observation: Two short_answer prompts state their own answers in plain English before asking for them. ch8-epox-diol-name says the OH groups are 'on opposite faces' and then asks for the term describing that relationship — the accepted answers are exactly 'anti' and 'trans', i.e. a synonym for the phrase already supplied. ch8-ozon-use says the fragments 'reveal exactly where the double bond was' and then asks the student to fill in the blank, with accepted answers 'location', 'position', 'placement'. Neither item requires any chemical reasoning; both are vocabulary substitutions off the stem.
findings.learner_impact: These are two of only four short_answer items and they generate no diagnostic signal — a student who understands nothing about epoxide opening or ozonolysis answers both correctly by paraphrase. Instructors get inflated mastery estimates on the epoxidation and ozonolysis concepts, and the chapter's stated ozonolysis objective ('use them to locate the original double bond') appears mastered when it was never tested.
findings.evidence: ch8-epox-diol-name prompt_text plus answer_key [redacted]; ch8-ozon-use prompt_text plus answer_key [redacted].
findings.recommended_outcome: These two items need stems that withhold the answer, so the student must supply the stereochemical relationship or the analytical inference rather than restate a phrase already given.

location.anchor_text: What is the stereochemistry of catalytic hydrogenation, and why?

findings.observation: All six nuggets author a practice_check (prompt plus answer), and none of them survives compilation: the string 'practice' appears zero times in the compiled reader chapter. The reader also contains no question blocks — the 32 compiled questions live only in compiled/question-set.json. The chapter a student actually opens is therefore six blocks of expository prose, twelve static molecules, one energy diagram, and two hidden empty videos, with no place to test themselves at any point.
findings.learner_impact: Students read six reaction mechanisms with zero interleaved retrieval, which is the reading pattern that produces confident fluency illusions and poor exam transfer. The authored practice_checks — which are well-targeted, especially 'What is the stereochemistry of catalytic hydrogenation, and why?' — are exactly what the reading needs and the student never sees them.
findings.evidence: topic.package.json nuggets[].practice_check present on all six nuggets (nugget-hydrogenation, nugget-hydroboration, nugget-epoxidation, nugget-dihydroxylation, nugget-ozonolysis, nugget-synthesis). grep -c 'practice' on frontend/public/reader/topic-chapters/alkenes-reactions-and-synthesis.json returns 0. No block in any section has a question/practice block_type.
findings.recommended_outcome: The reading surface needs the authored self-check items to reach the student in-line at the end of each section, so the chapter supports retrieval rather than continuous exposition.

location.anchor_text: Because boron is electron-deficient, it becomes bonded to the less hindered, less substituted carbon

findings.observation: This is the only causal explanation of anti-Markovnikov regiochemistry in the chapter, and it is a non-sequitur: boron's electron deficiency is why borane is electrophilic and adds at all, but it does not by itself explain why boron lands on the less substituted carbon. The two standard reasons — sterics (the bulky boron avoids the more substituted carbon) and, more importantly, the partial positive charge developing on the MORE substituted carbon in the four-centre transition state — are conflated into one clause, and the transition-state charge argument is absent entirely. The sentence effectively pairs an electronic premise with a steric conclusion.
findings.learner_impact: This is the concept whose own declared trouble_spot is 'Applying Markovnikov regiochemistry to an anti-Markovnikov reaction.' Students who learned from the prior chapter that electrophiles add so as to give the more stable carbocation will read 'boron is electron-deficient' and predict the opposite regiochemistry, because the chapter never explains why the same charge-stability logic that put H+ on the terminal carbon in HBr addition puts H on the internal carbon here. Without the TS argument, anti-Markovnikov becomes an arbitrary exception to memorize.
findings.evidence: nugget-hydroboration text.expanded, second paragraph; identical wording compiled into reader block blk-ketrqpgu. The hint ladders in ch8-hb-regio and ch8-hb-hotspot use only the steric framing ('Boron adds to the less hindered carbon'), so the electronic argument is nowhere in the chapter or its assessment.
findings.recommended_outcome: The regiochemistry needs a stated 'why' that connects to the carbocation-stability reasoning students already own — where the partial positive charge sits in the concerted transition state — so anti-Markovnikov reads as a consequence of the same principle rather than an exception to it.

location.anchor_text: "prerequisites": ["catalytic-hydrogenation"]

findings.observation: Two concepts declare prerequisites that do not match what their prose and questions assume. (1) oxidative-cleavage-ozonolysis lists catalytic-hydrogenation as its only prerequisite; there is no chemical dependency between them — nothing in the ozonolysis nugget uses hydrogenation. The real assumed knowledge is recognizing and naming aldehydes versus ketones, which is unlisted, yet the questions require the student to name acetone, acetaldehyde, pentanedial, butanal, 2-butanone and formaldehyde and to know that a fully substituted carbon gives a ketone. (2) alkene-synthesis-retrosynthesis lists only hydroboration-oxidation, syn-dihydroxylation and oxidative-cleavage-ozonolysis, but its own prose depends on acid-catalyzed hydration, halogenation and catalytic hydrogenation, and its questions (ch8-reagent-match-v2) grade HBr and Br2 outcomes. I verified the externally-referenced slugs (alkene-structure-pi-bond, markovnikov-hbr-addition, acid-catalyzed-hydration, alkene-halogenation-anti) all resolve correctly to the alkenes-structure-and-reactivity package, so the machinery works — these two entries are simply wrong.
findings.learner_impact: Any sequencing or remediation tool that trusts the prerequisite graph will route students to hydrogenation before ozonolysis (useless) and will not flag missing carbonyl nomenclature (the actual blocker for six ozonolysis questions). Students entering the synthesis section may not have hydration or halogenation activated, yet the section's entire argument is the complementary-pairs table built from them.
findings.evidence: concepts[4].prerequisites = ['catalytic-hydrogenation']; concepts[5].prerequisites = ['hydroboration-oxidation','syn-dihydroxylation','oxidative-cleavage-ozonolysis'] versus nugget-synthesis text.expanded 'Acid-catalyzed hydration gives the Markovnikov alcohol... Halogenation adds two halogens anti... Catalytic hydrogenation removes the double bond'. ch8-reagent-match-v2 grades l_br2 and l_hbr.
findings.recommended_outcome: The prerequisite graph needs to state what each section actually assumes — carbonyl recognition for ozonolysis, and the full set of complementary reactions for the synthesis section — rather than a nominal upstream link.

location.anchor_text: 2-Methyl-2-butene ((CH3)2C=CHCH3)

findings.observation: Three notation conventions drift across the chapter. (1) Nomenclature style is mixed: assets and prose use current IUPAC locants ('but-2-ene', 'butan-1-ol', '2-methylbut-2-ene', 'propane-1,2-diol') while questions use pre-1993 style ('1-Butene', 'cis-2-Butene', '2-Methyl-2-butene', '1,3-butadiene', '2-Butanone'). The same compound is 'mol-2-methylbut-2-ene' in the asset layer and '2-Methyl-2-butene' in ch8-ozon-products/ch8-ozon-draw. (2) cis/trans and E/Z are used interchangeably for the same structural class — ch8-hydrog-product and ch8-heat-of-hydrogenation-rank say 'cis-2-Butene'/'trans-2-Butene' while ch8-epox-product-v2 says '(E)-2-butene' — with no statement anywhere that they are equivalent here. (3) Subscript rendering is mixed inside a single answer list: ch8-antimarkovnikov-select-v2 offers 'OsO₄, then NaHSO₃' (Unicode) alongside 'cold, dilute KMnO4 (basic)' (plain), and ch8-synth-route offers 'BH₃.THF; then H₂O₂, NaOH' alongside 'dilute H3O+'.
findings.learner_impact: Students searching the reading for the compound named in a question ('2-Methyl-2-butene') will not find the figure that shows it ('2-methylbut-2-ene') and may believe they are different molecules. The unexplained cis/trans-versus-E/Z switch invites the belief that the epoxidation question is about a different kind of isomerism than the hydrogenation question. Mixed subscript rendering inside one option list reads as an authoring error and draws attention away from the chemistry being discriminated.
findings.evidence: assets[10].title 'Ozonolysis substrate: 2-methylbut-2-ene' versus ch8-ozon-products prompt_text '2-Methyl-2-butene'; ch8-heat-of-hydrogenation-rank cards 'cis-2-Butene'/'trans-2-Butene' versus ch8-epox-product-v2 prompt '(E)-2-butene'; ch8-antimarkovnikov-select-v2 options a/b; ch8-synth-route reagents r_hb/r_acid.
findings.recommended_outcome: The chapter needs one nomenclature convention, one stereodescriptor convention (or an explicit statement of equivalence at first use), and one subscript rendering applied uniformly across prose, figures and every option list.

location.anchor_text: Read in McMurry (OpenStax) — Chapter 8

findings.observation: The compiled reader declares mcmurry_chapter_number 8 and links students to the full OpenStax chapter 8, but the chapter (together with its stated companion, alkenes-structure-and-reactivity, whose six concepts I checked) covers only hydrogenation, hydroboration, epoxidation, dihydroxylation, ozonolysis, HBr addition, hydration and halogenation. Absent are halohydrin formation, oxymercuration-demercuration, carbene addition/cyclopropanation, radical addition and polymerization, biological additions, alkene preparation by elimination (which is what the word 'Synthesis' in the chapter title normally denotes), and the reaction-stereochemistry section that establishes racemic outcomes.
findings.learner_impact: An instructor who assigns this reader as chapter 8 will find roughly half of the sections in the linked textbook chapter unsupported, and students following the OpenStax link will encounter reactions the reader never mentions. The missing reaction-stereochemistry material is also the direct cause of finding instr-001. The title promise of 'Synthesis' is met only by a reagent-selection section, not by any route to making an alkene.
findings.evidence: Compiled reader mcmurry_chapter_number = 8, block blk-ne7x82ea links https://openstax.org/books/organic-chemistry/pages/8-why-this-chapter. concepts[] in this package (6) plus concepts[] in alkenes-structure-and-reactivity (alkene-structure-pi-bond, alkene-ez-stereochemistry, electrophilic-addition-carbocation, markovnikov-hbr-addition, acid-catalyzed-hydration, alkene-halogenation-anti).
findings.recommended_outcome: The chapter needs either coverage of the remaining chapter-8 transformations and the racemic-product principle, or an explicit scope statement to the instructor about which textbook sections it does and does not support, so assignment decisions are informed.

location.anchor_text: Predict the product of catalytic hydrogenation and identify its syn stereochemistry.

findings.observation: Two stated learning objectives are not assessed by any item that actually requires them. (1) nugget-hydrogenation's objective includes identifying syn stereochemistry, but its six questions test product identity (ch8-hydrog-product, -v2), H2 stoichiometry (ch8-hydrog-equiv, -v2) and alkene stability ranking (ch8-heat-of-hydrogenation-rank, -v2); none asks for a stereochemical product. The only place hydrogenation's syn character is graded is a single sorting card in ch8-stereo-categorize, which is filed under the dihydroxylation concept. (2) nugget-ozonolysis's objective 'use them to locate the original double bond' is assessed only by the fill-in-the-blank ch8-ozon-use, whose answer is the word 'location' — no item asks the student to work backward from a pair of carbonyl products to the parent alkene, which is the actual skill.
findings.learner_impact: Concept-level mastery reporting for catalytic-hydrogenation will read as mastered by students who cannot predict a syn product, and for ozonolysis by students who cannot run the analysis backward. The backward-inference skill is the one most likely to appear on an exam and is the one the chapter's own video brief (video-ozonolysis, storyboard step 3 'Recombine the fragments') was designed to teach — and that video compiles to an empty, hidden block.
findings.evidence: nuggets[0].learning_objectives; the six questions with concept_slug 'catalytic-hydrogenation'. nuggets[4].learning_objectives; ch8-ozon-use answer_key [redacted]. Compiled reader block blk-d83qw7fc has url '' and is_hidden true.
findings.recommended_outcome: Each concept needs at least one item that cannot be answered without exercising its stated objective — a stereochemical hydrogenation product, and a reverse-inference ozonolysis item that starts from the carbonyl fragments.

location.anchor_text: Wikipedia — Epoxidation with a peroxyacid

findings.observation: Four of the six 'background reading' links in the compiled reader are dead. I fetched all six: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catalytic_hydrogenation (200) and /wiki/Hydroboration-oxidation (200) resolve, but /wiki/Epoxidation_with_a_peroxyacid (404), /wiki/Syn_dihydroxylation (404), /wiki/Oxidative_cleavage_(ozonolysis) (404) and /wiki/Choosing_reactions_in_synthesis (404) do not exist. The URLs appear to have been generated mechanically from the concept titles rather than from real article names, which is why the last one — a slug derived from an internal pedagogical concept, not a chemical topic — could never have existed.
findings.learner_impact: Four of six sections offer the student a labelled 'Background reading' affordance that dead-ends. Students who are struggling are precisely the ones who click it, and they lose trust in the chapter's other external links, including the OpenStax assignment link that does work. An instructor who spot-checks one link and finds it fine will ship four broken ones.
findings.evidence: Compiled reader blocks blk-ato1wt8z, blk-e3lw8c4e, blk-8p0uocch, blk-4m78mkhx. curl HTTP status codes: 200, 200, 404, 404, 404, 404 for the six /wiki/ targets in section order.
findings.recommended_outcome: Every external reading link in the chapter needs to resolve to a real, on-topic page before publication, and the section whose concept has no encyclopedic counterpart needs no link at all rather than a fabricated one.

location.anchor_text: Show epoxidation as a single concerted step rather than a two-step ionic addition.

findings.observation: The one non-molecule figure in the chapter is a single-barrier energy profile whose spec contains one exergonic step and two minima labels ('Propene + peroxyacid', 'Epoxide + carboxylic acid'). It correctly shows the absence of an intermediate, but its stated learning goal is to establish the concerted mechanism, and the transition state — the butterfly TS in which the O–O bond breaks while both C–O bonds form — carries no label, no structure, and no annotation. The figure therefore conveys 'one hump' but not what is happening at the top of it.
findings.learner_impact: The declared trouble_spot for this concept is 'Treating epoxidation as a two-step ionic addition rather than a concerted transfer.' A student who sees one hump learns that there is no intermediate but still has no picture of simultaneous bond making and breaking, so the concerted claim remains a shape rather than a mechanism — and it is the single fact that explains the stereospecificity the chapter grades in ch8-epox-product-v2.

strengths: Structural fidelity is high: I machine-verified all 13 asset SMILES and every structure embedded in all 32 questions with RDKit — every one parses, and every molecular formula and InChIKey matches the compound its label claims (e.g. mol-2-methylbut-2-ene CC=C(C)C = C5H10, BKOOMYPCSUNDGP; mol-acetone CC(C)=O = C3H6O, CSCPPACGZOOCGX). The E/Z distractors in ch8-heat-of-hydrogenation-rank are correctly encoded (C/C=C\C = Z, C/C=C/C = E), and the cis/trans labels on the 2,3-dimethyloxirane options are chemically correct ((R,R) = trans, (R,S) meso = cis).

I re-derived every answer key independently and all intended chemical outcomes are correct: 2 equivalents of H2 for butadiene and for propyne, 1-butene and cyclopentene to butane/cyclopentane, propene and 2-methylpropene to the primary alcohols, 2-methylbut-2-ene to acetone plus acetaldehyde, cyclopentene to pentanedial (ring-opening, not two fragments), and the full acid-hydration-versus-hydroboration comparison matrices.

Assessment breadth is genuinely strong for a first version: 32 items across 11 question types (single_select, multi_select, numeric_with_units, rank_order, comparison_matrix, hotspot, short_answer, categorize_groups, structure_scaffold, synthesis_route, matching_pairs), every concept carries at least four items, and two structure_scaffold items require the student to draw a product rather than recognize one.

Feedback is diagnostic rather than generic: nearly every distractor carries a chemistry-specific explanation naming the misconception (e.g. ch8-ozon-products option c, 'Formaldehyde only forms from a terminal =CH2. This alkene has no =CH2 group'), and every item has a graduated two- or three-level hint ladder that narrows rather than reveals.

The complementary-pairs framing in nugget-synthesis (Markovnikov/anti-Markovnikov, syn/anti, add/cleave) is good synthesis pedagogy — it reduces reagent selection to two explicit decisions, regiochemistry and face, and the paired ch8-synth-route / ch8-synth-route-v2 items assess exactly that discrimination on the same substrate.

The cross-chapter prerequisite wiring is real, not decorative: I resolved alkene-structure-pi-bond, markovnikov-hbr-addition, acid-catalyzed-hydration and alkene-halogenation-anti and all four exist as concepts in the alkenes-structure-and-reactivity package.

personas.summary: Sentence by sentence this chapter is clear and correct, and the three authored detail tiers are a real kindness. But as compiled, it is six near-identical blocks of three dense paragraphs each, with no chapter overview, no summary, no worked example, no misconception callout, and zero practice inside the reading itself — every practice_check and every trouble_spot the author wrote was dropped in compilation. The chapter's entire point is which face a group is delivered to (syn vs anti), yet not one of its thirteen figures shows a face: they are flat SMILES structures of starting material and product, so 'same face' stays a phrase I have to take on faith. No reagent or intermediate is ever drawn — I am told a 'five-membered cyclic osmate ester' explains syn addition and a peroxyacid has a 'weak, electrophilic oxygen–oxygen bond', but I never see either. The question bank is worse for a student like me: hints hand over the answer instead of unsticking me (level 2 for ch8-hydrog-product is literally the product), the correct choice is the first option in all ten single-selects and the given order in every rank/match/categorize item, so I can score well by guessing position, and several graded items (bromonium anti addition, anti epoxide opening, 9-BBN, alkyne hydrogenation) test content this chapter never contains. I would read this, feel like I understood it, and then discover on the exam that I only memorized sentences.

location.anchor_text: the two hydrogen atoms are transferred to the same face of the double bond

findings.observation: Syn vs anti — 'which face the groups are delivered to' — is the organizing idea of all six sections, but no figure in the chapter shows a face, a wedge/dash, or any three-dimensional relationship. All thirteen molecule blocks are flat 2D line structures of a substrate and a product with no stereochemistry in the SMILES (mol-butane 'CCCC', mol-propane-1-2-diol 'CC(O)CO', mol-methyloxirane 'CC1CO1'). The asset mol-butane even carries the learning_goal 'Identify the alkane formed by syn addition of H2 to but-2-ene', but butane drawn as CCCC cannot display syn anything.
findings.learner_impact: I cannot picture 'same face'. I convert it into a word I memorize — 'hydrogenation = syn' — with no mental image behind it, so when a question shows a ring or an (E)-alkene and asks for the stereochemical outcome I have nothing to reason from and I guess. This is the single place I would form a durable wrong mental model (that syn/anti is a label attached to reagents rather than a geometric fact).
findings.evidence: Reader blocks blk-u0agrki8, blk-kw1rj1ri, blk-v7kbfya4, blk-1u0rwpbn, blk-g0qp30q7; package assets mol-hydrog-butene, mol-butane, mol-propene-diol, mol-propane-1-2-diol. Prose asserting the geometry: 'both oxygen atoms are delivered to the same face' (nugget-dihydroxylation), 'both new carbon–oxygen bonds form at the same time and on the same face' (nugget-epoxidation).
findings.recommended_outcome: A learner needs to actually see the two faces of a specific alkene and see two groups arriving on one of them versus on opposite ones, for at least one worked substrate, rather than inferring geometry from the word 'face'.

location.anchor_text: Bromine addition (Br₂) through a bromonium ion

The word 'anti' as an addition mode appears exactly once in the whole reader ('the anti addition seen in halogenation'), never defined, in a section about a reaction the chapter does not teach. I scroll back through all six sections looking for the missing paragraph, do not find it, conclude the fault is mine, and either guess or stop. On a term that appears in the correct-answer group label itself ('Anti (opposite faces) addition'), I learn the definition from the quiz after being graded on it.

findings.recommended_outcome: Either the chapter must teach anti addition (back-side opening of a cyclic intermediate, with halogenation/bromonium and acidic epoxide opening) before grading it, or those items must be scoped to what the chapter actually contains. A term must be defined in the reading before it is scored.

location.anchor_text: Adding H-H across CH2=CHCH2CH3 gives CH3CH2CH2CH3.

findings.observation: The hint ladders end by handing over the answer rather than by unsticking the reasoning. ch8-hydrog-product level 2 states the product; ch8-ozon-use-v2 level 2 is 'Its formula is O3' when the answer is 'ozone/O3'; ch8-epox-diol-name-v2 level 2 is "Its common name starts with 'epox...' and its IUPAC parent is 'oxirane'" when the accepted answers are epoxide/oxirane; ch8-stereo-categorize level 2 is the complete answer key ('H2/Pd and OsO4 are syn; bromonium opening and epoxide opening are anti'); ch8-reagent-match and ch8-antimarkovnikov-select-v2 level 2 likewise restate the full key; ch8-ozon-draw level 3 is 'Draw (CH3)2C=O, acetone.'
findings.learner_impact: Hints are the first thing a low-confidence student reaches for. Two clicks gets me the answer, I type it, I get a green check, and I have practiced nothing — I leave believing I know the material. The one scaffold built for me is the one that most reliably prevents me from learning.

findings.recommended_outcome: Hint ladders need to stay procedural to the last rung — pointing at the next decision to make (which carbon is less substituted? which face did the cyclic intermediate occupy?) — so a stuck student is moved forward without the answer being conceded.

location.anchor_text: Applying Markovnikov regiochemistry to an anti-Markovnikov reaction

findings.observation: Every concept carries an authored trouble_spot naming exactly the wrong move a student makes, and not one of them appears in the compiled reader. 'Applying Markovnikov regiochemistry to an anti-Markovnikov reaction', 'Assigning anti stereochemistry to a syn addition', 'Keeping the carbon skeleton intact instead of cleaving the double bond', 'Treating epoxidation as a two-step ionic addition rather than a concerted transfer', 'Forgetting that both hydrogens are delivered to the same face' — the prose states the correct fact each time but never names the mistake or warns me against it.
findings.learner_impact: These are precisely the errors I make, and I only find out I made them after being graded on them (the wrong-answer explanations are where the traps are finally named). Nothing in the reading interrupts me at the moment I am forming the wrong idea, so I carry it into the quiz and then into the exam.

location.anchor_text: For example, 2-methylbut-2-ene is cleaved to acetone and acetaldehyde.

findings.observation: The chapter contains no worked example. Its only instance of a procedure being carried out is the single sentence 'For example, 2-methylbut-2-ene is cleaved to acetone and acetaldehyde' — the result with none of the intermediate steps (locate the C=C, cut it, cap each former alkene carbon with =O, decide aldehyde vs ketone from the H count). The reverse use, which the chapter advertises ('identifying the carbonyl products of cleavage reveals the position of the original double bond, since the two fragments join at the carbons that had been doubly bonded'), is never demonstrated on any example at all; the only place it is worked is a storyboard line in video_brief video-ozonolysis, whose video block has an empty url and is_hidden true. Students are then asked to execute both procedures cold in ch8-ozon-draw (draw the ketone), ch8-ozon-use, and ch8-synth-route.

On the draw item I open a blank canvas with nothing to model, and I go straight to the hints (which then give me the answer, see stud-003).

location.anchor_text: form a five-membered cyclic osmate ester, so both oxygen atoms are delivered to the same face

findings.observation: Every causal explanation in the chapter rests on a species that is never drawn. The cyclic osmate ester is the entire reason dihydroxylation is syn; mCPBA's 'weak, electrophilic oxygen–oxygen bond' is the entire reason a peroxyacid transfers oxygen; the organoborane is the entire reason the OH ends up where boron was; the ozonide is the species the workup cleaves. None of OsO4, mCPBA, BH3, the organoborane, the osmate ester or the ozonide has a structure asset anywhere in the package — the thirteen molecule figures are all substrates and final products.

I cannot check whether a five-membered ring across one face is even geometrically possible, so I stop trying to understand and fall back to memorizing reagent→product pairs — which is exactly the strategy that collapses on ch8-hydration-compare, where I am asked to reason about mechanism (carbocation vs concerted) rather than recall products.

location.anchor_text: The complementary pairs established across these two chapters make the choice explicit.

location.anchor_text: The (CH3)2C= end of the alkene becomes a ketone: acetone, (CH3)2C=O.
