On ch8-ozon-draw, a student who draws acetaldehyde (the other, equally valid fragment, just not the one asked for) gets the same paragraph as a student who drew an alcohol, and both are simply told the answer is acetone.
findings.learner_impact: When I get one of these wrong I never find out *what I did* wrong — whether I cut the bond in the wrong place, mixed up aldehyde and ketone, or misread which product was requested. I copy the given answer, cannot diagnose my own error, and repeat it next time.
findings.evidence: compiled/question-set.json: ch8-hydrog-equiv, ch8-hydrog-equiv-v2, ch8-epox-diol-name, ch8-epox-diol-name-v2, ch8-ozon-draw, ch8-ozon-draw-v2, ch8-ozon-use, ch8-ozon-use-v2 all have wrong_answer_explanations: [].
findings.recommended_outcome: The open-response items need error-specific feedback for their predictable wrong answers (wrong fragment, wrong carbonyl class, wrong equivalence count) so a wrong attempt diagnoses the misstep instead of just revealing the key.

location.anchor_text: Show epoxidation as a single concerted step rather than a two-step ionic addition.

findings.observation: The chapter's only non-molecule figure is a one-step energy profile whose stated learning goal is to show epoxidation 'as a single concerted step rather than a two-step ionic addition' — but no two-step profile appears anywhere in the chapter for it to contrast with, and the figure carries no numbers, only 'barrier: medium'. A single hump with two labelled minima cannot by itself convey 'not two steps' to someone who does not already know what a two-step profile looks like.
findings.learner_impact: I see one hill and take away 'reactants go to products', which I already knew. The distinction the figure exists to make — the epoxidation trouble_spot, 'Treating epoxidation as a two-step ionic addition' — passes me by entirely, and I have no way to tell whether one hump means one step or just a simplified drawing.
findings.evidence: Asset rc-epoxidation spec.steps = single exergonic step, barrier 'medium'; reader block blk-hnpaxwq5; concept alkene-epoxidation trouble_spot 'Treating epoxidation as a two-step ionic addition rather than a concerted transfer'.
findings.recommended_outcome: A one-step profile only teaches 'concerted' against a visible two-step alternative; the learner needs the contrast made explicit rather than implied by a lone diagram.

location.anchor_text: 2-methylbut-2-ene is cleaved to acetone and acetaldehyde

findings.observation: The same compounds are named differently between the reading and the questions with no bridge: the prose and asset say 'but-2-ene' and '2-methylbut-2-ene' while the questions say 'cis-2-Butene' and '2-Methyl-2-butene'; the ozonolysis workup is 'zinc and aqueous acid' in the expanded tier, 'zinc in acid' in the standard tier, and 'Zn/H2O' in every question. Additionally, the two surfaced ozonolysis items (ch8-ozon-products, ch8-ozon-draw) use the identical substrate and identical answer as the prose's one-line example.
findings.learner_impact: I do not reliably know that 2-methylbut-2-ene and 2-methyl-2-butene are the same molecule, so I spend working memory re-deriving the name instead of doing the chemistry, and I second-guess whether Zn/H2O is the workup I read about. And because the graded ozonolysis items reuse the sentence I memorized, I pass them without ever transferring the skill to a new substrate.
findings.evidence: Asset mol-2-methylbut-2-ene title vs ch8-ozon-products/ch8-ozon-draw prompt_text; nugget-ozonolysis _detail_texts standard ('zinc in acid') vs expanded ('zinc and aqueous acid') vs question wording ('Zn/H2O'); ch8-ozon-draw answer_key 'CC(C)=O' = the prose example's product.
findings.recommended_outcome: One naming convention across prose, figures and questions (or an explicit equivalence note), and at least one surfaced ozonolysis item on a substrate other than the worked example.

location.anchor_text: Wikipedia — Choosing reactions in synthesis

findings.observation: The 'Background reading' Wikipedia URLs appear to be generated mechanically from concept titles rather than from real article names: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Choosing_reactions_in_synthesis, /wiki/Epoxidation_with_a_peroxyacid, /wiki/Syn_dihydroxylation, /wiki/Oxidative_cleavage_(ozonolysis), /wiki/Hydroboration-oxidation. 'Choosing reactions in synthesis' is a chapter section heading, not an encyclopedia topic, and the others do not match Wikipedia's actual article titles. Five of the six sections carry one of these as their only supplementary help; only section 1 also has the OpenStax link.
findings.learner_impact: When I am stuck, the link labelled 'Background reading' is what I click. Landing on a 'Wikipedia does not have an article with this exact name' page at the moment I am already struggling is where I stop working and switch to memorizing the reagent list — and it quietly costs the chapter its only per-section escape hatch to an explanation in different words.
findings.evidence: Reader blocks blk-6ybo2gd3, blk-n9buxh42, blk-ato1wt8z, blk-e3lw8c4e, blk-8p0uocch, blk-4m78mkhx; only blk-ne7x82ea (nugget-hydrogenation) links to OpenStax.
findings.recommended_outcome: Every outbound 'background reading' target needs to resolve to a real page before publication, and each section needs at least one working alternate explanation to fall back on. (I could not fetch the URLs from this environment — see open_questions.)

strengths: Three genuine detail tiers (terse / standard / expanded) are authored for every one of the six sections, and the reader exposes them through a detail-level slider — a student who is drowning can shorten the text without losing the section.

The prose itself is plain, unhedged and jargon-light at the sentence level; each section states the transformation, the reagent and the stereochemical outcome in that order, which is a predictable and learnable shape.

Wrong-answer explanations on the multiple-choice and matrix items are specific rather than generic — 'That is the Markovnikov product you would get from acid-catalyzed hydration' (ch8-hb-regio) and 'Formaldehyde only forms from a terminal =CH2. This alkene has no =CH2 group' (ch8-ozon-products) name the actual misstep.

ch8-hydration-compare and ch8-reagent-match force the cross-reaction comparison that the chapter is really about, rather than testing one reaction in isolation — these are the two items that would most help me if the underlying prose supported them.

Every molecule figure carries alt text and a learning_goal, and concept-level prerequisites and trouble_spots are explicitly authored — the pedagogical intent is present in the package even where it does not reach the compiled reader.
open_questions: Does the question runtime shuffle option, card and match order at delivery? If it does, stud-004's positional pattern is mitigated; as authored in compiled/question-set.json the key is fully predictable from presentation order.
Are nugget practice_check items meant to compile into the reader as blocks? They are authored on all six nuggets and appear nowhere in the compiled chapter, which is what drives stud-005.

Is the 32-item question set intended to be reachable from the reader chapter, or only from a separate assessment surface? Both artifacts are available:false, so I could not tell what a student's actual practice path is.

Are outbound external_link URLs validated at compile time? I had no network access to confirm the Wikipedia targets in stud-017 return real articles; that finding's confidence reflects the pattern of the URLs, not a fetch.

Are the 16 '-v2' staged variants ever shown to students, or are they reserve items? Several of my concerns (propyne/alkyne in ch8-hydrog-equiv-v2, the picture-only-on-the-correct-answer cue in ch8-diol-syn-v2) sit in variants, and their severity depends on whether a student ever sees them.

personas.summary: The reading side of this chapter is genuinely accessible: every reaction's regiochemistry and stereochemistry is carried in prose (three detail levels), no figure is a sole carrier of meaning, the twelve molecule figures are simple enough that their one-line alt text is a fair equivalent, and the platform renderers behind all eleven question types are keyboard-complete (rank_order has Move up/down buttons, matching/categorize/comparison_matrix use selects, the route builder uses selects, hotspot atoms are real buttons, and both structure_scaffold items correctly set typed_structure_entry='allowed' with a SMILES answer key). The assessment side, however, fails badly on answer-leak neutrality: nine of the thirty-two authored questions have an accessible_description that states the answer outright — the two draw items name the product molecule ('Draw acetone, (CH3)2C=O'), both hotspot items name the atom to select, three short-answer items list their accepted answers, and both synthesis_route items map each reagent to the product it gives. None of these are caught by the compile-time guard, which only matches answer ids, verdict vocabulary, and computed numbers. Compounding this, the hotspot items have no neutral non-visual orientation at all: the rendered structure carries alt='Structure for this question' and the atom buttons are labelled only 'C atom 1'..'C atom 4', so once the leak is removed a screen-reader user has no way to map atom index to chemical position — the item becomes uncompletable rather than merely hard. The reaction-coordinate figure's alt text also under-describes what is drawn, and the two video briefs carry no transcript or audio-description plan. Publication should be blocked until the leaks and the hotspot orientation gap are fixed.

location.anchor_text: Draw acetone, (CH3)2C=O, the ketone formed when 2-methyl-2-butene undergoes ozonolysis.

findings.observation: Both structure_scaffold items name the exact product a student is being asked to draw inside accessibility_bundle.accessible_description. ch8-ozon-draw's description is 'Draw acetone, (CH3)2C=O, the ketone formed when 2-methyl-2-butene undergoes ozonolysis' against answer_key.smiles 'CC(C)=O'; ch8-ozon-draw-v2's is 'Draw acetaldehyde, CH3CHO, the aldehyde formed when 2-methyl-2-butene undergoes ozonolysis' against answer_key.smiles 'CC=O'. The prompts themselves say only 'Draw the KETONE product' / 'Draw the ALDEHYDE product'.
findings.learner_impact: A screen-reader user is handed the graded answer before attempting the item, so the question measures nothing for them and their attempt data is invalid; instructors who notice will disable the accessible description rather than the leak, which is worse. This escapes the compile guard because answer_key.smiles is not under an answer-marked key name and 'CC(C)=O' is not id-like, so nothing fails the build.
findings.evidence: topic.package.json question_sets ch8-ozon-draw accessibility_bundle.accessible_description vs answer_key [redacted]; ch8-ozon-draw-v2 vs {
}. Mirrored into compiled/question-set.json unchanged.
findings.recommended_outcome: Both draw items need a non-visual description that conveys the task and the stimulus (which alkene, which fragment is wanted, that typed SMILES entry is available) without naming or drawing the product; the graded chemistry must still have to be reasoned out non-visually.

location.anchor_text: select the terminal CH2 carbon of the double bond, which becomes the carbon bearing OH

findings.observation: Both hotspot items state which atom to select. ch8-hb-hotspot: 'On a structure of 2-methylpropene, select the terminal CH2 carbon of the double bond, which becomes the carbon bearing OH after anti-Markovnikov hydroboration-oxidation' (answer atom_0). ch8-hb-hotspot-v2: 'On a structure of propene, select the terminal CH2 carbon, which becomes the carbon bearing OH after anti-Markovnikov hydroboration-oxidation'. The prompt asks only 'click the carbon atom that ends up bearing the -OH group'.
findings.learner_impact: The entire cognitive task — deciding which carbon boron adds to — is performed for the screen-reader user. The guard does not fire because the description never contains the literal id 'atom_0'.
findings.evidence: topic.package.json ch8-hb-hotspot / ch8-hb-hotspot-v2 accessibility_bundle vs answer_key.correct_option_ids [redacted].
findings.recommended_outcome: The hotspot descriptions need to convey the stimulus structure and the selection task only, with the regiochemical decision left to the student.

location.anchor_text: Type the word describing what ozonolysis reveals about a double bond in an unknown alkene: its location or position.

findings.observation: Three short-answer items list their own accepted answers in the accessible description. ch8-ozon-use ends '...: its location or position' against answer_text ['location','position','placement']; ch8-ozon-use-v2 ends '...: ozone, O3' against answer_text ['ozone','o3','o_3']; ch8-epox-diol-name-v2 ends '...formed by epoxidation: epoxide or oxirane' against answer_text ['epoxide','oxirane',...]. By contrast ch8-epox-diol-name (the base item of that pair) is correctly neutral, which shows the authoring standard was known and inconsistently applied.
findings.learner_impact: Screen-reader users receive the graded fill-in answer verbatim. The guard misses all three: 'location'/'position'/'epoxide'/'oxirane' are not in VERDICT_VOCABULARY, and 'o3' is under three characters so it is not treated as id-like.
findings.evidence: topic.package.json ch8-ozon-use, ch8-ozon-use-v2, ch8-epox-diol-name-v2 accessibility_bundle vs their answer_key.answer_text arrays.
findings.recommended_outcome: These three descriptions need to state what the student must supply (a one-word term, a reagent name) without enumerating the accepted strings — matching the neutral pattern already used in ch8-epox-diol-name.

location.anchor_text: hydroboration-oxidation gives the primary alcohol; acid hydration gives the secondary alcohol; hydrogenation gives butane

findings.observation: Both synthesis_route descriptions supply the full reagent-to-product mapping the student is being graded on. ch8-synth-route: '...hydroboration-oxidation gives the primary alcohol; acid hydration gives the secondary alcohol; hydrogenation gives butane', where the prompt already identifies the target as 'butan-1-ol (a primary alcohol)' — so the description names the correct reagent by construction. ch8-synth-route-v2 does the same for the secondary-alcohol target.
findings.learner_impact: A screen-reader user only has to pattern-match the target descriptor already in the prompt to the mapping in the description; no retrosynthetic reasoning is required. Sighted students must recall the regiochemistry. Guard misses it because the leak is semantic, not an id or number.
findings.evidence: topic.package.json ch8-synth-route / ch8-synth-route-v2 accessibility_bundle vs answer_key.accepted_routes [[{reagent_id r_hb, product_id m_1ol}]] and [[{r_acid, m_2ol}]].
findings.recommended_outcome: Both route items need a description that lists the available reagents and candidate products as an inventory of the workspace, without asserting which reagent produces which product.

findings.observation: The hotspot items give a screen-reader user no neutral way to identify the atoms. HotspotActivityRenderer renders the structure image with a fixed alt of 'Structure for this question' and labels each atom button only as `${symbol} atom ${index+1}` — 'C atom 1', 'C atom 2', 'C atom 3' for C=CC. Nothing in the question package maps an atom index to its position in the molecule. Today the only text that does so is the leaked answer flagged in access-002; once that leak is removed (as it must be) there is no non-visual path to a correct selection at all.
findings.learner_impact: A blind or low-vision student either gets the answer for free or cannot answer at all — never a valid attempt. The buttons are keyboard-reachable and correctly use aria-pressed, so this is not an operability failure; it is a missing equivalent for the structure the interaction is performed on.
findings.evidence: [internal source reference — not in this repo] lines ~236 (alt="Structure for this question") and ~268 (aria-label={`${atom.symbol} atom ${atom.index + 1}`}); topic.package.json ch8-hb-hotspot student_config [redacted] and ch8-hb-hotspot-v2 {
} carry no per-atom description; answer_key.correct_option_ids [redacted].
findings.recommended_outcome: Both hotspot items need a neutral, question-scoped connectivity readout that ties each selectable atom index to its chemical environment (substituents, which two atoms are the double-bond carbons) so a non-visual learner can reason to a selection — supplied without stating which atom is correct.

location.anchor_text: Single-step energy profile for concerted peroxyacid epoxidation of propene, with one barrier from reactants to the epoxide.

findings.observation: The chapter's only non-molecule figure is described by a single sentence that omits most of what the rendered diagram shows. The spec declares energy_axis 'free_energy', an 'exergonic' step, minima_labels ['Propene + peroxyacid', 'Epoxide + carboxylic acid'], and minima_molecules that draw the propene and methyloxirane structures on the diagram itself. The alt text names none of the axis, neither minimum label, the fact that products sit below reactants, the medium barrier, or the two inline structures, and carries no schematic/not-to-scale caveat. The asset has no long_description, even though the reader renders one when present (ReaderBlockRenderer StructureCard/ReactionCoordinateCard) and falls back to it entirely when a learner turns images off.
findings.learner_impact: A screen-reader user, or any learner reading with images suppressed, gets the concerted/one-barrier point but loses the thermodynamic reading (exergonic, products lower) and the labelled species — which is the part of the figure that goes beyond what the prose already says. The alt text does carry the figure's stated learning goal, so this is a degradation rather than a total loss.
findings.evidence: topic.package.json assets rc-epoxidation spec + accessibility.alt_text; frontend reader block blk-hnpaxwq5 renders 'Described as: {alt_text}' with no long_description present.
findings.recommended_outcome: This diagram needs a fuller text equivalent covering axis meaning, both labelled minima and the structures drawn at them, the downhill (exergonic) direction, the single barrier, and a not-to-scale caveat — the level of detail the twelve simple molecule figures do not require.

location.anchor_text: Place the two products side by side to make the regiochemical complement explicit.

findings.observation: Neither video brief carries a transcript, caption text, or audio-description plan. video-hydration-complement's storyboard is purely spatial ('Place the two products side by side to make the regiochemical complement explicit') while its narration_outline never names a structure ('State that the two reactions give opposite regiochemistry'); video-ozonolysis is the same shape. As compiled, both reader video blocks (blk-1kcvkqh6, blk-d83qw7fc) have url:"" and is_hidden:true, and their 'description' is a verbatim production storyboard line ('Start from 1-butene and show acid-catalyzed hydration giving butan-2-ol') rather than learner-facing text.
findings.learner_impact: Nothing is broken for students today because the blocks are hidden, but as briefed these videos would ship with narration that talks over the structures instead of describing them, and with no caption or transcript track — leaving deaf/hard-of-hearing and blind learners without the regiochemical comparison the video exists to make. The storyboard's meaning is carried entirely by spatial arrangement.
findings.evidence: topic.package.json video_briefs video-hydration-complement and video-ozonolysis (storyboard, narration_outline, formats mp4/gif, status needs_review); compiled reader blocks blk-1kcvkqh6 and blk-d83qw7fc with empty url and is_hidden true.
findings.recommended_outcome: Before either video is produced, each brief needs a narration/caption plan in which the spoken track itself names the structures and the change being shown, plus a time-independent text equivalent for the side-by-side comparison, and the reader block needs a learner-facing description rather than a storyboard instruction.

location.anchor_text: "text": "OsO₄, then NaHSO₃", "structure_smiles": "OC1CCCC1O"

findings.observation: Structure images are attached to some answer options and not others, and in ch8-diol-syn-v2 only the correct option carries one: option a ('OsO₄, then NaHSO₃') has structure_smiles 'OC1CCCC1O' — a picture of the target diol — while the two distractors have none. ch8-diol-syn has structures on options a and c but not b. SelectedResponseRenderer sets the option image alt to option.text, so a screen-reader user never learns that a structure was shown at all.
findings.learner_impact: Sighted students get a visual cue (the only illustrated reagent, showing the product being asked about) that non-visual students cannot perceive, so the two populations are answering different questions. The accessible_description correctly enumerates all three options, which makes the asymmetry invisible to the compile checks.
findings.evidence: topic.package.json ch8-diol-syn-v2 student_config.options and ch8-diol-syn student_config.options; [internal source reference — not in this repo] line ~173 alt={option.text}.
findings.recommended_outcome: Option-level illustration needs to be consistent within an item and must not sit only on the key; where a structure genuinely carries information, its content needs to reach non-visual users rather than being aliased to the option label.

location.anchor_text: one mole of 1,3-butadiene, which contains two double bonds

findings.observation: The accessible description performs the graded counting step: 'Enter the number of moles of hydrogen needed to fully hydrogenate one mole of 1,3-butadiene, which contains two double bonds', where the answer is 2.0 equiv and hint level 1 is 'One mole of H2 is needed per carbon-carbon double bond.' A sighted student must parse CH2=CH-CH=CH2 from the prompt to reach the same count. The paired variant ch8-hydrog-equiv-v2 handles this correctly ('which contains one triple bond' against an answer of 2), so the neutral pattern exists.
findings.learner_impact: Screen-reader users skip the one inference the item tests. The guard's number check does not fire because the count is written as the word 'two' and because '2' also appears in the student_config placeholder.
findings.evidence: topic.package.json ch8-hydrog-equiv accessibility_bundle vs answer_key [redacted] and feedback_bundle.hints level 1.
findings.recommended_outcome: This description needs to render the condensed formula in a screen-reader-parsable way without stating how many double bonds it contains.

location.anchor_text: H2/Pd and OsO4 are syn; bromonium opening and epoxide opening are anti.

findings.observation: Across the set, the final hint routinely states the complete answer key rather than a last scaffold: ch8-stereo-categorize level 2 gives all four assignments; ch8-stereo-categorize-v2 level 2 gives all four; ch8-reagent-match-v2 level 2 gives all four pairs ('BH3 = primary alcohol; H3O+ = secondary alcohol; Br2 = dibromide; HBr = one Br'); ch8-antimarkovnikov-select-v2 level 2 resolves every option; ch8-hydrog-product level 2 writes out the product formula. Only the two draw items use a three-level ladder where the bottom-out answer arrives at level 3.
findings.learner_impact: This matters disproportionately for learners who rely on hints as a processing support rather than a reasoning nudge — students with reading, attention or working-memory differences open hints routinely, and here the second click ends the item instead of unblocking it. It also removes the diagnostic value of hint telemetry for exactly those students.
findings.evidence: topic.package.json feedback_bundle.hints for ch8-stereo-categorize, ch8-stereo-categorize-v2, ch8-reagent-match, ch8-reagent-match-v2, ch8-antimarkovnikov-select-v2, ch8-diol-syn-v2, ch8-hydrog-product.
findings.recommended_outcome: The multi-item sorting and matching questions need an intermediate rung between 'general principle' and 'here is the key' — a partial worked case or a decision rule applied to one item — so a student using hints as an access support still completes the reasoning.

location.anchor_text: Hydrogenation substrate: but-2-ene

findings.observation: Heading levels skip a rank in every section of the compiled chapter. TopicPackageChapterRenderer emits the chapter title as h1 and each section title as h2, while ReaderBlockRenderer emits every figure, video and link card heading as h4 — there is no h3 anywhere. With five sections and roughly twenty h4 cards, the chapter's outline is h1 > h2 > h4 throughout.
findings.learner_impact: Screen-reader users navigating by heading level, or using a headings list to skim, get a structure that misreports nesting depth; the figure cards appear two levels below their section rather than one. This is a rendering-layer defect that this chapter's data cannot fix on its own, but it manifests in every section here.
findings.evidence: [internal source reference — not in this repo] lines 172 and 195 (h1, h2); [internal source reference — not in this repo] lines 188, 304, 382, 404, 515, 542, 586 (all as="h4").
findings.recommended_outcome: The reader's block-card headings need to sit one level below the section heading so the chapter exposes a continuous outline; flag to platform rather than to chapter authoring.

strengths: Every stereochemical and regiochemical claim in the chapter is carried in prose, not in a picture: syn delivery from the catalyst surface, boron at the less-substituted carbon, the concerted single-face oxygen transfer, the cyclic osmate ester, and the cleavage-to-carbonyls rule are all stated in the standard and expanded nugget texts, so no non-visual learner depends on a figure to learn the chemistry.

The three detail levels (terse / standard / expanded) are compiled into the reader as _detail_texts and swapped by the personalization preference, giving learners with reading or attention differences a real density control rather than an all-or-nothing toggle.

Both structure_scaffold items correctly set student_config.typed_structure_entry='allowed' with a SMILES answer key, which is the platform's declared keyboard-complete path for drawing questions — no required activity in this chapter is pointer-only.

The renderers behind all eleven question types in this set are keyboard-operable: rank_order exposes per-card Move up/Move down buttons with an aria-live position readout instead of drag-only reordering, matching_pairs and categorize_groups use labelled selects, comparison_matrix cells are selects with per-cell accessible names, synthesis_route uses selects and buttons, and hotspot atoms are real buttons with aria-pressed rather than color-only selection state.
Nothing in the chapter uses color, motion, or hover as a sole carrier of meaning; there are no animations requiring pause/step controls, and all option distinctions are stated in the option text.

For the twelve simple molecule figures (three to five heavy atoms, no stereocentres drawn), the one-line alt text is a genuinely sufficient equivalent — these need no longer description, and adding one would be redundant.
ch8-epox-diol-name and ch8-hydrog-equiv-v2 show correctly neutral accessible descriptions, demonstrating that the leaking descriptions elsewhere are an inconsistency rather than an absent standard.
open_questions: The compiled reader question manifest (frontend/public/reader/topic-chapters/alkenes-reactions-and-synthesis.questions.json) keeps only slug/title/type/prompt_text and strips student_config, answer_key, feedback_bundle and accessibility_bundle for all 16 surfaced questions. The same is true of the alkyl-halide and epoxides chapters, so this looks like an intentional manifest-only shape — but it means the authored accessible_description never reaches a reader-surface learner. Which surface actually consumes accessibility_bundle: LMS/LTI delivery only, or is a reader question player planned?

ch8-hb-hotspot's answer key is 'atom_0' while HotspotActivityRenderer announces buttons as one-based ('C atom 1'). Is the index-to-label offset guaranteed stable across the RDKit render path, and does the correct atom always come out as index 0 for these SMILES? If not, a non-visual learner reasoning to 'the terminal CH2' could still select the wrong button.

Do the ozonolysis and hydration/hydroboration videos have a production caption or audio-description workflow attached elsewhere, or does status 'needs_review' with formats mp4/gif mean they would ship from these briefs as-is?

I used category 'assessment-readiness' for the hint-ladder finding (access-010) because the rubric assigns no category to hint giveaways; it is a listed id, so no new category was coined, but a future rubric revision may want an explicit one.

personas.summary: This is a reactions chapter in which no reaction is drawn. All 13 assets are standalone flat structures (12 `molecule` cards plus one single-step reaction coordinate); the compiled reader contains zero `reaction` blocks even though the reader's block renderer supports them (ReaderBlockRenderer case "reaction" with reaction_smiles). Every transformation therefore reaches the student as two or three vertically stacked, unconnected structure cards, with the reagents (Pd/C, BH3 then H2O2/NaOH, mCPBA, OsO4 then NaHSO3, O3 then Zn) living only in prose. The chapter's central stereochemical claims — syn delivery of H2, syn addition of H and OH, stereospecific epoxidation, syn (cis) diol — are asserted in every nugget and named in the concepts' own trouble_spots, yet no figure carries a wedge, a dash, a face, or a stereocenter; worse, the chosen examples are ones in which syn/anti is structurally unshowable (but-2-ene to butane has no stereocenter; propene to propane-1,2-diol and propene to 2-methyloxirane each give a single stereocenter). Both planned videos compile to `url: ""` with `is_hidden: true`, so they render as nothing and the two comparisons they carried (hydration vs. hydroboration; fragment-to-alkene-carbon mapping in ozonolysis) exist nowhere visually. In the question bank the visual quality is uneven: the two hotspot items and the (E)-2-butene epoxidation item are genuinely structure-dependent and good, but two single_select items attach a rendered structure only to the correct option, and one of those renders ethane-1,2-diol for an option whose text claims 'syn (cis)'. The chapter's prose is clear; the figure layer is doing far less work than the content demands.

location.anchor_text: H2 adds across a carbon–carbon double bond to give an alkane

findings.observation: No transformation is drawn anywhere in the chapter. All six sections present a reaction as two or three separate `molecule` cards stacked vertically (substrate card, then product card[s]) with no arrow, no reagent label, and no visual link between them. The compiled reader block census is molecule 13, text 6, external_link 6, video 2 (both hidden), mcmurry_link 1, reaction_coordinate 1 — zero `reaction` blocks, despite ReaderBlockRenderer supporting a `reaction` block type that renders reaction_smiles through StructureCard.
findings.learner_impact: A student scanning the page sees a gallery of unrelated structures rather than six transformations. The reagent that defines each reaction (Pd/C, BH3·THF then H2O2/NaOH, mCPBA, OsO4 then NaHSO3, O3 then Zn) is recoverable only by reading the paragraph above the figures, so the figures cannot be used for review, and nothing on the page distinguishes 'propene becomes an epoxide' from 'here are two molecules'. This puts the entire explanatory burden back on prose in exactly the chapter whose subject is change.
findings.evidence: Reader blocks blk-u0agrki8 (but-2-ene) / blk-kw1rj1ri (butane); blk-2zpgo66v (1-butene) / blk-udsl7aee (butan-1-ol); blk-di3wpm1j (propene) / blk-g0qp30q7 (2-methyloxirane); blk-v7kbfya4 / blk-1u0rwpbn; blk-yzju274m / blk-lnqcar4u / blk-97kxjcdh. Every one is block_type "molecule" with a bare SMILES and a caption; none carries reagents or an arrow.
findings.recommended_outcome: Each of the six transformations needs to be legible as a transformation at a glance — substrate, reagent/conditions, and product visually joined — rather than as adjacent independent structures whose relationship exists only in prose.

location.anchor_text: both hydroxyl groups lie on the same face — a syn, or cis, diol

findings.observation: Every stereochemical claim in the chapter is told and never shown, and the specific examples chosen make it unshowable. Hydrogenation's syn delivery is illustrated with but-2-ene (CC=CC, no E/Z specified) going to butane (CCCC), a product with no stereocenter at all. Syn dihydroxylation is illustrated with propene going to propane-1,2-diol (CC(O)CO), a single stereocenter formed as a racemate, where 'both OH on the same face' has no visible referent. Epoxidation's stereospecificity is illustrated with propene going to 2-methyloxirane (CC1CO1), again one stereocenter. Hydroboration's syn addition ends at butan-1-ol (CCCCO), an achiral primary alcohol. Not one asset SMILES in the package contains a stereo descriptor.
findings.learner_impact: The stereochemical distinction is the graded outcome of four of the six concepts and is named verbatim in their trouble_spots ('Forgetting that both hydrogens are delivered to the same face (syn)', 'Assigning anti stereochemistry to a syn addition'). A student who works from the figures sees flat structures that are equally consistent with syn and anti addition, so the misconception the chapter names is the one the figures reinforce. The word 'syn' becomes a term to memorize rather than a spatial fact to see.
findings.evidence: assets mol-hydrog-butene (CC=CC) / mol-butane (CCCC); mol-propene-diol (CC=C) / mol-propane-1-2-diol (CC(O)CO); mol-propene-ep (CC=C) / mol-methyloxirane (CC1CO1); mol-1-butene / mol-butan-1-ol (CCCCO). Concept trouble_spots for catalytic-hydrogenation and syn-dihydroxylation. Nugget text: 'the two new carbon–hydrogen bonds are formed on the same side'; 'the two hydroxyl groups are syn (cis)'.
findings.recommended_outcome: The syn/anti distinction needs at least one worked case per stereochemical claim in which the two faces are actually distinguishable in the drawn structure — which requires substrates (internal or cyclic alkenes) whose products can express the relationship, not just an added notation on the current examples.

location.anchor_text: Two routes to an alcohol: hydration versus hydroboration

findings.observation: Both video blocks compile to empty and render nothing. blk-1kcvkqh6 (hydroboration section) and blk-d83qw7fc (ozonolysis section) each have content.url = "" and is_hidden = true; ReaderBlockRenderer returns null on block.is_hidden, so the student sees no video, no poster, and no text stub. Their `description` fields are also truncated to storyboard step 1 only ('Start from 1-butene and show acid-catalyzed hydration giving butan-2-ol.'), losing steps 2 and 3 of each brief.
findings.learner_impact: The two comparisons these briefs were designed to carry are the two the chapter most needs and now shows nowhere: the Markovnikov / anti-Markovnikov contrast from one alkene, and the mapping of ozonolysis fragments back onto the original alkene carbons. Because the block renders as literally nothing rather than as a described placeholder, a learner has no signal that a planned explanation is missing, and neither does an instructor previewing the chapter.
findings.evidence: video_briefs video-hydration-complement (status needs_review, storyboard 3 steps) and video-ozonolysis (status needs_review); compiled blocks blk-1kcvkqh6 and blk-d83qw7fc with url "" and is_hidden true; [internal source reference — not in this repo]
findings.recommended_outcome: Either the two planned explanations need to reach the student in some form, or the chapter needs to not carry blocks that silently vanish; the regiochemistry contrast and the fragment-to-carbon mapping need a visible home regardless of whether motion is ever produced.

location.anchor_text: A syn (cis) 1,2-diol

findings.observation: In ch8-diol-syn the correct option a is labelled 'A syn (cis) 1,2-diol' but renders structure_smiles "OCCO" — ethane-1,2-diol, which has no stereocenters and therefore cannot be syn or anti. Option b ('An anti (trans) 1,2-diol') carries no structure at all, and option c (epoxide) carries "C1CO1". So the item asks a student to choose a stereochemical outcome while showing a picture that cannot express stereochemistry, next to a distractor with no picture.
findings.learner_impact: A student reading the drawn option learns that 'syn diol' looks like HOCH2CH2OH — a structure with no faces — which actively undercuts the concept the item assesses. The mixed render (two of three options drawn) also makes the option set visually incoherent, so structure and text carry contradictory information at the moment of decision.
findings.evidence: compiled/question-set.json, ch8-diol-syn student_config.options: a {text: 'A syn (cis) 1,2-diol', structure_smiles: 'OCCO'}, b {text: 'An anti (trans) 1,2-diol'} (no structure), c {structure_smiles: 'C1CO1'}. Same pattern in ch8-diol-syn-v2, where option a 'OsO₄, then NaHSO₃' renders 'OC1CCCC1O' — cyclopentane-1,2-diol with no stereo — for a prompt that asks specifically for cis-cyclopentane-1,2-diol.
findings.recommended_outcome: Where an item's answer is a stereochemical relationship, the rendered structures must be able to express that relationship (or no structure should be rendered on any option); a picture that contradicts its own label needs to go.

location.anchor_text: Which reagent system converts cyclopentene into cis-cyclopentane-1,2-diol?

findings.observation: In both ch8-diol-syn and ch8-diol-syn-v2 a rendered structure is attached only to the correct option. In v2 the options are reagent systems; option a ('OsO₄, then NaHSO₃', correct) carries structure_smiles 'OC1CCCC1O' while options b (mCPBA then aqueous acid) and c (O3 then Zn) carry no structure. In v1, of the three options only the correct one and one distractor are drawn.
findings.learner_impact: The figure becomes a visual answer cue: a student who cannot reason about the chemistry can select the only option that renders a picture. This inflates measured mastery on precisely the syn-dihydroxylation concept the chapter flags as a trouble spot, and it teaches students to answer from layout rather than structure.
findings.evidence: compiled/question-set.json ch8-diol-syn-v2 student_config.options — only option 'a' has structure_smiles; answer_key [redacted]. ch8-diol-syn — options a (correct) and c drawn, option b undrawn; answer_key [redacted].
findings.recommended_outcome: Option rendering within a single item needs to be uniform so that the presence of a structure carries no information about correctness.

location.anchor_text: the two fragments join at the carbons that had been doubly bonded

findings.observation: The ozonolysis section shows three unconnected cards — 2-methylbut-2-ene, acetone, acetaldehyde — with nothing indicating that the two carbonyls are co-products of one cleavage, which alkene carbon became which product, or where the bond broke. The analytic use stated in the prose ('identifying the carbonyl products reveals the position of the original double bond') depends entirely on that mapping, and the ozonide intermediate named in the prose is never drawn.
findings.learner_impact: Three stacked structures read equally well as 'three possible products'. Students who must run the logic backwards — which the chapter assesses in ch8-ozon-use and in the analytic framing of the nugget — have no picture of the join to reason from, so the reverse direction is memorized as a rule instead of read off a diagram.
findings.evidence: Reader blocks blk-yzju274m, blk-lnqcar4u, blk-97kxjcdh in section nugget-ozonolysis; nugget-ozonolysis expanded text; the only asset that would have shown the mapping (video-ozonolysis storyboard step 3, 'Recombine the fragments to show how the products identify the original alkene') compiles hidden — see visual-003.
findings.recommended_outcome: The correspondence between each alkene carbon and its carbonyl fragment — in both directions — needs to be visible on the page, including which end gives the ketone and which the aldehyde.

location.anchor_text: boron adds at the less substituted carbon

findings.observation: The two-stage nature of hydroboration–oxidation is invisible in the figures: only 1-butene and butan-1-ol are drawn. The organoborane intermediate, the position boron takes, the separate H2O2/NaOH oxidation step, and the retention of configuration at that carbon are all prose-only. The Markovnikov counterpart (butan-2-ol, mol-butan-2-ol) exists in the package but is placed four sections later in nugget-synthesis, so the contrast the section text makes is never visible in the section that makes it.
findings.learner_impact: The concept's own trouble_spot is 'Applying Markovnikov regiochemistry to an anti-Markovnikov reaction' — a discrimination between two products of the same alkene. Showing one product alone gives the learner nothing to discriminate against at the point of instruction, and the reason for the outcome (where boron goes) has no visual anchor. The chapter assesses the contrast directly in ch8-hydration-compare and ch8-synth-route.
findings.evidence: nugget-hydroboration asset_ids = [mol-1-butene, mol-butan-1-ol]; mol-butan-2-ol assigned to nugget-synthesis only; nugget text 'boron becomes bonded to the less hindered, less substituted carbon, and hydrogen adds to the more substituted carbon on the same face'.
findings.recommended_outcome: Where boron lands, and how that fixes the alcohol's position relative to acid-catalyzed hydration, needs to be visible at the point the contrast is taught — not only in a later section.

location.anchor_text: The complementary pairs established across these two chapters make the choice explicit.

findings.observation: The closing synthesis section states three complementary pairs in a single dense paragraph (hydration vs. hydroboration–oxidation; halogenation anti vs. dihydroxylation syn; hydrogenation vs. ozonolysis) and carries exactly two figures — butan-1-ol and butan-2-ol. There is no chapter-level summary that shows all six reactions, their reagents, and their regio/stereo outcomes in one spatial arrangement.
findings.learner_impact: This section's task is selection among reactions, which is inherently a comparison across the whole chapter, and the chapter is assessed that way (ch8-reagent-match matches four reagents to four product classes; ch8-antimarkovnikov-select and its v2 span three reactions). A learner doing that task has to hold six transformations in memory from six separate scrolled sections, because nothing on the page lays them side by side.
findings.evidence: nugget-synthesis expanded text (three complementary pairs in one paragraph); nugget-synthesis asset_ids = [mol-butan-1-ol, mol-butan-2-ol]; reader section nugget-synthesis contains blk-aghq6md3 (text), blk-hals58lj, blk-jtotl7f7, blk-4m78mkhx.
findings.recommended_outcome: The chapter needs one place where all of its reactions, reagents, and regio/stereo outcomes can be compared simultaneously rather than recalled sequentially.

location.anchor_text: the heat of hydrogenation, provides a quantitative measure of the relative stability of isomeric alkenes

findings.observation: Heat of hydrogenation as a stability measure is asserted in one prose sentence with no figure, yet it is assessed at 'advanced' difficulty by a three-card ranking item (ch8-heat-of-hydrogenation-rank: 1-butene, cis-2-butene, trans-2-butene, ranked by heat released) and again in ch8-heat-of-hydrogenation-rank-v2. The argument is that isomers converging on the same product sit at different starting energies — a relationship about relative levels. The chapter contains a reaction_coordinate asset type (rc-epoxidation), so the energy-diagram capability is present but is not applied here.
findings.learner_impact: Ranking three isomers by ΔH requires holding the 'same product, different starting heights' picture in the head; a student who cannot construct that picture from one sentence is left ranking by a memorized substitution rule, which is exactly what v2 then also tests. The strongest available support for the item is absent from the section it assesses.
findings.evidence: nugget-hydrogenation expanded text, final paragraph; questions ch8-heat-of-hydrogenation-rank (cards with structure_smiles C=CCC, C/C=C\\C, C/C=C/C; correct_order 1-butene > cis > trans) and ch8-heat-of-hydrogenation-rank-v2; nugget-hydrogenation asset_ids = [mol-hydrog-butene, mol-butane] only.
findings.recommended_outcome: The relative-energy relationship among isomeric alkenes converging on one alkane needs to be visible, not inferred from a single sentence, given that the chapter grades it.

location.anchor_text: Show epoxidation as a single concerted step rather than a two-step ionic addition.

findings.observation: The chapter's only energy diagram states its purpose as distinguishing concerted from stepwise, but it shows only one profile: a single exergonic step with a generic 'medium' barrier, no transition-state structure or label, and no two-step profile to contrast against. Its minima_labels name 'Propene + peroxyacid' and 'Epoxide + carboxylic acid' while minima_molecules draws only 'CC=C' and 'CC1CO1' — the peroxyacid and the carboxylic acid byproduct named in the labels are never drawn.
findings.learner_impact: A single hump does not read as 'concerted' to a student who has not already internalized what a two-step profile looks like — the meaning of one barrier is only available by comparison. The unlabeled maximum also skips the one image that actually carries concertedness (both C–O bonds forming at once at the transition state), which is the specific misconception the concept records: 'Treating epoxidation as a two-step ionic addition rather than a concerted transfer'.
findings.evidence: asset rc-epoxidation spec: steps [{type: 'exergonic', barrier: 'medium'}], minima_labels ['Propene + peroxyacid', 'Epoxide + carboxylic acid'], minima_molecules {0: 'CC=C', 1: 'CC1CO1'}; concept alkene-epoxidation trouble_spots; compiled block blk-hnpaxwq5.
findings.recommended_outcome: The 'one step, not two' point needs to be readable as a contrast and needs the transition state to be identified; a lone unlabeled barrier does not carry the claim it is captioned with.

location.anchor_text: Classify each alkene reaction by whether the two new groups are delivered to the same face (syn) or to opposite faces (anti).

findings.observation: Several items whose answers are inherently spatial or structural are entirely text-only. ch8-stereo-categorize sorts four reactions into syn vs. anti with no structure anywhere. ch8-hydration-compare includes the row 'Adds H and OH to the same face (syn addition)' with zero structures in the item. ch8-reagent-match and ch8-reagent-match-v2 match reagents to product classes ('Epoxide', 'Vicinal (1,2-) dibromide', 'Primary (anti-Markovnikov) alcohol') with no structures on either column. ch8-ozon-draw and ch8-ozon-draw-v2 give the substrate only as condensed text '(CH3)2C=CHCH3' next to a blank canvas, so a student must parse a linear formula before drawing.
findings.learner_impact: These items can be answered by matching remembered phrases ('OsO4 → syn') without ever picturing a face or a product, so they measure vocabulary recall rather than the structural understanding stated in the objectives — and they give students no structural feedback loop. In the draw-the-product items the substrate parsing is an extra, unrelated obstacle stacked in front of the assessed skill.
findings.evidence: compiled/question-set.json: ch8-stereo-categorize (0 structure_smiles), ch8-hydration-compare (0), ch8-reagent-match / -v2 (0), ch8-antimarkovnikov-select / -v2 (0), ch8-ozon-draw / -v2 (student_config [redacted], 0 structures). Of 32 compiled questions, 14 contain no rendered structure of any kind.
findings.recommended_outcome: Items that assess a spatial or structural outcome need the structural information present in the item, so the answer comes from reading chemistry rather than from recalling a phrase pairing.

location.anchor_text: Two molecules of propanal

findings.observation: Multi-molecule options use inconsistent conventions and one renders a structure that contradicts its own text. In ch8-ozon-products-v2, option b reads 'Two molecules of propanal' but structure_smiles is 'CCC=O' — a single molecule will be drawn. In ch8-ozon-products, the analogous multi-product options use dot-separated fragment SMILES ('CC(C)=O.CC=O', 'CCC(C)=O.C=O'), which do render two species.
findings.learner_impact: A distractor whose picture shows one molecule while its text says two either quietly signals that the option is wrong or teaches an incorrect reading of the drawing. In a cleavage question, 'how many product molecules' is precisely the discrimination being tested.
findings.evidence: compiled/question-set.json ch8-ozon-products-v2 option b {text: 'Two molecules of propanal', structure_smiles: 'CCC=O'}; compare ch8-ozon-products option a {structure_smiles: 'CC(C)=O.CC=O'}.
findings.recommended_outcome: Option text and option structure need to agree on species count, using one consistent convention for multi-product answers across the bank.

location.anchor_text: Line structure of propene, a three-carbon chain with a terminal double bond.

findings.observation: Alt texts describe connectivity only and never the teaching point of the figure. mol-propene-ep and mol-propene-diol carry byte-identical alt text although they appear in sections where different features matter (the site of oxygen transfer vs. the two carbons that gain OH). None of the 13 alt texts names which carbon gains the new group, which bond breaks, or which face is involved. This matters more than usual here: the renderer's images-off path (applyPrefs / textEquivalentBlock in [internal source reference — not in this repo]) converts each figure into a callout built from long_description or alt_text, and no asset in this package has a long_description — so alt text becomes the whole figure.
findings.learner_impact: A learner who turns images off (or reads the alt) gets a structure inventory rather than the transformation, which compounds visual-001: with figures suppressed the chapter's six reactions reduce to twelve descriptions of unrelated line structures. Flagging for the Accessibility persona to dedupe.
findings.evidence: assets mol-propene-ep and mol-propene-diol have identical smiles 'CC=C' and identical accessibility.alt_text; no asset in topic.package.json defines long_description; [internal source reference — not in this repo] textEquivalentBlock() falls back to alt_text.
findings.recommended_outcome: Each figure's description needs to carry the point that figure is captioned with (its learning_goal), not just the molecule's connectivity — especially since the description is the entire figure when images are off.

location.anchor_text: Line structure of butane, a four-carbon chain with only single bonds.

findings.observation: Several cards add nothing beyond their own caption. mol-butane (CCCC), mol-acetaldehyde (CC=O) and the duplicated propene pair (mol-propene-ep / mol-propene-diol, identical SMILES and alt text) occupy full-width structure cards whose content is fully conveyed by the name already printed on the card. The chapter is thirteen figures long and none of them is annotated, so the figure layer is high in count and low in information density.
findings.learner_impact: Scrolling past near-empty cards trains a learner to skip figures, which costs attention that the one or two figures carrying real information (the epoxidation profile) need. The same rendering budget spent on drawn transformations would carry far more.
findings.evidence: assets mol-butane, mol-acetaldehyde, mol-propene-ep and mol-propene-diol (both 'CC=C' with identical alt_text); reader blocks blk-kw1rj1ri, blk-97kxjcdh, blk-di3wpm1j, blk-v7kbfya4.
findings.recommended_outcome: Isolated single-species cards that restate their own captions should be absorbed into the transformation they belong to or dropped, rather than retained as standalone figures.

strengths: ch8-hb-hotspot and ch8-hb-hotspot-v2 are genuinely structure-dependent: the student selects an atom on a rendered molecule (molecule_smiles 'C=C(C)C' and 'C=CC', correct answer atom_0), so the regiochemical answer must be read off a structure rather than recalled as a phrase.

ch8-epox-product-v2 is the one place in the chapter where stereochemistry is actually drawn — trans and cis 2,3-dimethyloxirane as distinct rendered options [SMILES redacted] — and it shows the package is capable of stereochemically explicit figures.
ch8-heat-of-hydrogenation-rank cards carry structures including explicit E/Z SMILES (C/C=C\C, C/C=C/C), so the cis/trans distinction the ranking depends on is visible on the cards.
ch8-synth-route renders start structure, target structure, and all three candidate products (5 structures), making the retrosynthetic choice a comparison between drawn molecules.
Every figure block carries alt_text, and the reader's images-off path preserves it as a described callout rather than dropping the block, so suppressing figures does not silently delete content.

Each figure card carries a per-asset learning_goal as its description, so no figure is decorative or purposeless on its face; and because no figure uses overlaid annotation, no label obscures any structure.
All 13 authored assets surface in the compiled reader (13 molecule blocks including one intentional reuse of butan-1-ol, plus the reaction coordinate) — no orphaned or dropped figure assets.
open_questions: Are the two video blocks (blk-1kcvkqh6, blk-d83qw7fc) intentionally staged as hidden pending production, or is url = "" a compile defect? Both video_briefs are status 'needs_review', which suggests staging, but the reader gives the student no placeholder either way.

Should a rendered structure appearing only on the correct option (visual-005, ch8-diol-syn and ch8-diol-syn-v2) count as an answer leak under the schema's blocker definition? I scored it high rather than blocker; the orchestrator may want a standing policy on visual answer cueing.

Does ReactionCoordinateCard actually render spec.minima_molecules inline in the reader? Whether rc-epoxidation shows propene and the epoxide at its minima changes how much of visual-010 remains after any TS labeling.

Three of the six Wikipedia external_link URLs look auto-generated from concept titles and are unlikely to resolve: /wiki/Syn_dihydroxylation, /wiki/Epoxidation_with_a_peroxyacid, /wiki/Choosing_reactions_in_synthesis. Outside my persona's remit (not a figure), but it affects the supporting-visual pathway students are pointed to, and only one section carries an OpenStax link.

publishing.available is false and science_review.status is 'not_reviewed' — I reviewed this as a pre-publication draft; if any of the flat-structure choices in visual-002 were deliberate scope decisions (deferring stereochemistry to a later chapter), that intent is not recorded anywhere in the package.

executive_summary: Baseline verdict: blocked. The chemistry is structurally sound — the instructor persona machine-verified all 13 asset SMILES and every structure in all 32 questions by formula and InChIKey and re-derived every answer key's intended outcome — but two graded items are chemically wrong as depicted (a single enantiomer keyed as THE epoxidation product of an achiral+achiral reaction; ethylene glycol labelled 'a syn (cis) 1,2-diol'), one blocker-level teach-before-grade gap spans five facts the chapter never contains, nine accessible_descriptions hand screen-reader users the graded answer (all invisible to the compile-time guard), and the hotspot items lose their only non-visual path the moment those leaks are fixed. Both rank_order items ship pre-solved and the whole bank is positionally predictable. The chapter is also the fourth confirmed instance of the recompile-revert class: [commit ref — not in this repo]'s four Wikipedia link fixes and [commit ref — not in this repo]'s hydroboration regiochemistry fix lived only in the compiled artifact and are absent from the package — the live reader 404s on 4 of 6 links today. The deepest instructional finding is unanimous across personas: this is a reactions chapter in which no reaction is drawn — every transformation is two unlinked flat structure cards, no intermediate or reagent is depicted, and all three syn-stereochemistry claims are illustrated on substrates where stereochemistry is invisible.
consensus_strengths: Structural fidelity: all 13 asset SMILES and every question structure verify by formula and InChIKey; every answer key's intended chemical outcome re-derives correctly (both machine-checked).
Assessment breadth: 32 items across 11 question types with every concept covered by at least four items, including two draw items and two synthesis-route items.
Both structure_scaffold items set typed_structure_entry 'allowed' with SMILES keys — the ch5 chapter-authored access blocker does not recur, and all eleven renderers in use are keyboard-complete.
Three genuine prose detail tiers are authored for all six sections, and the sentence-level prose is plain, correctly ordered (transformation, reagent, outcome), and chemically accurate.
Diagnostic distractor feedback on the selected-response items names the actual misstep rather than restating the key.
The complementary-pairs synthesis framing (regiochemistry x face x add/cleave) is genuinely good pedagogy, and cross-chapter prerequisite slugs all resolve to real ch7 concepts.

ranked_recommendations.title: ch8-epox-product-v2 keys a single enantiomer as THE product of an achiral+achiral reaction
ranked_recommendations.need: Epoxidation of achiral (E)-2-butene with achiral mCPBA must give the racemic (2R,3R)+(2S,3S) trans epoxide; the item keys one drawn enantiomer as the product and offers no way for a student reasoning to the other enantiomer to be right, and the racemate principle is taught nowhere in the prose.
ranked_recommendations.rationale: Least-complex full fix: reframe the option texts to name the trans product as racemic (both enantiomers, one drawn as representative), keep the meso cis distractor, and add one prose sentence stating that achiral reactants cannot deliver a single enantiomer. No new asset needed.

ranked_recommendations.title: ch8-diol-syn labels ethylene glycol 'syn (cis)' and illustrates only answer-adjacent options
ranked_recommendations.need: The keyed option's drawn structure (OCCO) has no stereocenters and cannot be syn; option illustration is asymmetric across the pair (v2 illustrates ONLY the key), so the one item introducing the syn-diol concept teaches a false visual and cues the answer non-chemically.
ranked_recommendations.rationale: The item must be re-based on a substrate where syn/anti is expressible (cyclopentene -> cis vs trans cyclopentane-1,2-diol with verified stereo-SMILES) with every option treated identically; a label fix alone would leave the discrimination unillustrable.

A student who mastered the chapter still misses these items and cannot tell whether the gap is theirs.

ranked_recommendations.title: Nine accessible_descriptions state the graded answer

ranked_recommendations.title: Both rank_order items ship pre-solved and the whole bank is positionally predictable
